0.title: high above the farm
0.shot1: Before the song. The air at the altitude of a low-flying aircraft, out over open summer farmland. Scattered white fair-weather clouds stand at this height and below, drifting slowly past, their tops flat-lit and their undersides a cool grey-green, and the land shows through the gaps between them: fields in pale sage and olive rectangles, a dirt track ruled across them, hedge lines, one row of trees. In one of those gaps sits a single farm, small enough to cover with a thumbnail - the farmhouse, the cow barn, the chicken coop with its ridged corrugated tin roof, the chicken-wire fence ruled right around the yard, and at the bottom corner of the yard a pond barely three metres across, a dark green oval the size of a lentil at this distance. Nothing on the farm is large enough to read from up here: no animal and no person resolves, and nothing down there moves. The clouds keep passing, the farm stays where it is, and the ground never comes any closer.

cameras.v1: [Push in, slow, small] An aerial from the altitude of a low-flying aircraft, looking down at a steep angle, cloud tops passing through the near frame. The farm sits small in the lower middle at the start and settles to the centre. The camera holds its altitude for the whole clip and never descends; by the last second the angle has come round to almost straight down and the shot settles and stops there, the whole property inside the frame with the pond at its bottom corner - the framing the next clip has to begin on.
cameras.v2: [Truck right, slow, small] High oblique with the cloud tops in the lower frame and the far horizon and open sky in the upper third, the farm a small mark on the land between them, so the height reads as height and not as a map.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Insert on one cloud top passing, close enough that its flat lit shoulder and cool underside fill most of the frame, with the field pattern small and sharp through the gap beside it.

1.title: the pond from above
1.shot1: The farm lies still around its pond. The house, the barn, the chicken coop and the fenced yard sit in about forty metres of ground, and at the bottom corner of it is one small farm pond, barely three metres across, its green water skinned with duckweed. From straight overhead the chicken-wire fence reads as a thin dark line ruled right around the yard and the coop as a small rectangle of ridged tin, and neither of them is ever missing from the plan. In the water there is at first only a small dark shape, no bigger against the property than a seed. It resolves into a common pond frog - eight centimetres from nose to rump, the length of a man's thumb, forty of his own body lengths from the far bank. He kicks both back legs out and together in a slow swimming stroke and jerks forward on each push, gliding to a stop between kicks, the way a frog actually moves through water. His head stays above the surface and leaves a small spreading wake. He covers half the distance to the bank. Nothing else on the farm moves. At the bottom corner of the pond, no bigger than a seed himself, the crown of a straw hat and the shoulders under it sit motionless on a folding chair, seen from straight above, so there is nothing of the man but the hat brim and his shoulders, with the shadow of the chair beside them.

cameras.v1: [Pedestal down, slow, large] A straight-down aerial plan view that begins on exactly the framing the previous clip ended on: the whole property inside the frame - house, barn, chicken coop, the fenced yard, the fence line and the fields around them - the pond one small dark oval near the bottom and the frog a single dark speck on the water no wider than a few pixels. From there the camera descends through the air toward the pond, losing altitude the whole way while it stays pointed straight down, so the buildings grow and slide out past the edges of the frame one after another until the pond alone fills it and the speck has become a readable frog seen from above, about a twentieth of the frame wide. The angle never tilts, no horizon and no sky ever enter the frame, and the farm buildings stay flat roof-plans below the camera the whole way down.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Wide at eye level from the bank, the whole yard and the coop behind the water, so the place reads as a place and not a diagram. The frog is a small green mark out on the pond, no taller in frame than a blade of the grass in the foreground.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Close on the water surface, tight enough that the duckweed leaves read as separate discs and the frog's 8 cm body crosses about half the frame.

2.title: swimming toward the farm
2.shot1: The frog makes slow, jerky swimming strokes across the open water. Flies circle around him and he ignores them completely, holding his course toward the farm buildings that stand blurred with distance ahead of him. Ahead across the water the cracked mud of the bank rises, the leaning chicken-wire fence runs along the top of it, and the ridged tin roof of the coop shows behind the fence to the right. He reaches the bank.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] Over the frog's shoulder, right down at the waterline, the farm ahead of him.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] The answering angle from ahead of him at the same water level, the pond behind.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Close on his face just above the water, flies crossing it.

3.title: hauling out of the water
3.shot1: The frog plants his arms on the bank and heaves himself out of the pond, slack and heavy with water. The bank is dry mud cracked into flat plates with black lines between them. He flops onto his belly in the grass and stays there, face down, not moving. Above and behind him the leaning chicken-wire fence sags between its posts, torn open in places and worn away underneath at one point into a gap his size. Far off at the other end of the bank, at the very edge of frame, a man on a folding chair leans right down over a notebook, the brim of his straw hat flat across his face so none of it can be read, and the shadow of the chair lies on the mud beside him. He takes no notice.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] Profile, at ground level in the gap between bank and water.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Three-quarter front and low, so the effort reads on his face.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Extreme close on his hands gripping the muddy bank.

4.title: rolling onto his back
4.shot1: The frog lies face down in the grass. Nothing about him moves except his back, rising and falling as he pants and breathes out, exhausted. Then one effortful swing and he rolls onto his back, and lies there looking straight up at the sky.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] Straight down on the whole frog in the grass, close, held.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Wide at eye level, the frog small in the grass with the pond behind.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Close on his back alone, rising and falling.

5.title: sitting sad by the pond
5.lyrics: Ich sitze traurig am Rand vom Teich
5.shot1: The frog's eyes are glassy and unfocused, the blue sky and one thin drifting cloud faintly reflected across them. He sings the line.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] Close on the frog's face.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Wide from across the water, the frog small at the near bank.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] The reverse - the sky and moving clouds he is staring into.

6.title: wet skin in sunlight
6.lyrics: Meine Haut ist glibschig und trotzdem weich
6.shot1: The frog lies stretched out in the grass, his skin catching the sunlight and shining wet from head to foot, green and speckled, the pale belly soft. He sings the line.

cameras.v1: [Tracking shot] At grass height, travelling slowly along him from head to foot.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] High and looking down on the same pose, which makes him small.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Extreme close on one patch of wet skin as the light moves over it.

7.title: licking his own eye
7.lyrics: Die Fliegen schwirren um mein Gesicht, ich könnt' sie fressen aber Hunger hab ich nicht
7.shot1: Flies circle the frog's face. He unrolls his tongue slowly, not to catch anything, but to wipe it across his own eyeball like a gecko. Then another tired, heavy exhale. He sings the line.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] Extreme close on the frog's face, flies crossing the frame.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Wide, the frog small in the grass, the flies invisible at this size.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Close on the flies themselves turning in the air above him.

8.title: the hen house in the distance
8.shot1: The frog rolls back onto his belly and props his chin tiredly on his hands. His gaze goes out across the yard to a hen house standing in front of the cow barn. It is five metres off - sixty of his own body lengths, which from down here is the far side of the world - beyond the sagging chicken-wire fence and its worn gap, its corrugated tin roof ridged against the sky, soft and pale behind the heat off the ground. At the edge of the frame the same man is still there by the water, head bowed over the notebook with the straw hat brim covering his face. Neither of them has ever noticed the other.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] Profile at grass height, the hen house small past him in the distance.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Over his shoulder, past his head, so the hen house is the subject.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Close on his eyes, fixed on something far off.

9.title: the hen pecking grain
9.lyrics: Sie sagt meine Augen sind zu groß
9.shot1: A sandy-tan hen walks slowly and proudly about the yard, pecking grain out of the dirt, taking no notice of anything else. The frog sings the line.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] Wide, the hen centred in the yard with room around her.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Medium on the hen, chest up, walking through frame.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Insert on her beak taking grain out of the dirt.

10.title: the hen in his eyes
10.shot1: The hen is reflected small and sharp in the frog's eyes, which stare after her with open longing.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] Extreme close on the frog's eyes, filling the frame.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Wide, both of them in one frame with the distance between them.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] The reverse - the hen as he is seeing her, small and far off.

11.title: the hen turns away
11.lyrics: Sie hasst Amphibien, was ist da los
11.shot1: The hen works over a patch of dirt with her beak, then lifts her head and looks off toward the pond. She turns away with complete indifference and walks off in a hen's stiff strut, leaving the patch of ground empty behind her.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] From behind the hen at ground level, locked off; she walks out of frame and the empty ground stays.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Front on the hen, so her indifference is readable on her face.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Close on her scaly feet working the dirt.

12.title: back to the frog
12.shot1: The frog is still lying on the cracked mud by the pond, looking straight ahead at nothing. Cattails stand at the edge of frame and the leaning chicken-wire fence runs along the bank behind him.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] The same locked frame as before, focus travelling back across to the pond.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Wide on the pond and the frog lying at its edge.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Close on the frog's face, looking at nothing.

13.title: i am a frog
13.lyrics: Ich bin ein Frosch! Was soll ich tun?
13.shot1: The frog sings the line and hammers one fist down into the grassy ground, desperate and furious.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] Close, front on, eye level.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Wide, the frog alone by the pond with the whole yard around him.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Insert on the fist coming down into the grass.

14.title: in love with a chicken
14.lyrics: Bin argh verknallt in ein Huhn. / Uns’re Welten, weit auseinander. / Doch bestimmt nur für einander.
14.shot1: The frog sits with his fist pressed flat against the middle of his chest, in the overwrought way of anime melodrama. His eyes are closed and he looks down as he sings the line. The sky behind and above him is left completely empty - an even, unbroken summer blue, no cloud shapes, nothing in it - because something is placed there later.
14.shot2: Nothing in the staging changes. The frog opens his eyes and a single tear glitters in the corner of one of them as he looks up at the empty sky. He sings the line.
14.shot3: The frog wipes the tear out of his eye and his expression sets, stubborn. He sings the line, then gathers himself and sets off hopping through the grass.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] Profile, dead side on, the frog to the right of frame facing left, sky behind him.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Three-quarter front, where his face reads best.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Extreme close on the fist held flat against his chest.

composite.where: upper left of the sky, half transparent: the hen seen in profile
composite.note: the screenplay says oben links. The element is generated: 90_hen-profile-element, same 226 frames as this plate.

15.title: imagine our children
15.shot1: Full frame, and this clip is composited into the sky later, so it is staged as its own complete shot and not as a faded inset. The hen sits on a plain wooden chair, crocheting, the hook working steadily. The view widens off her and three small Federphibien come into it, on the floor in front of the chair, playing with plush tadpole toys. He sings the line.

cameras.v1: [Zoom out] Starting close on the hen and her crochet hook and widening until the three Federphibien on the floor are in frame.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Low at floor level among the Federphibien and their plush tadpoles, the hen and the chair behind them.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Insert on the crochet hook working in her beak.

composite.where: into the open sky in the upper half of scene 16, half transparent
composite.note: one of the three Zukunftsvisionen - the hen crocheting while three Federphibien play

16.title: hopping through the grass
16.shot1: The frog hops along on a steady repeating cycle, the same push and land over and over at an even rhythm, and he fills about a third of the frame. He is only crossing five metres of ground in the whole song, in small hops, so the painted background drifts past behind him slowly and at a perfectly constant rate. This is built to LOOP: it ends on exactly the pose and the background position it started on, so the clip can be butt-joined to itself and run as long as it needs to. Nothing in the grass or the background is distinctive enough to give the repeat away - no landmark, no single recognisable weed, no change of light. He never leaves the frame and nothing enters it. Above him the upper half stays open sky with nothing in it at all.

cameras.v1: [Tracking shot] Travelling alongside him at his own height, matching his speed exactly so he holds the same spot in the lower third and the sky stays open above him.
cameras.v2: [Tracking shot] Travelling with him from slightly behind and lower, the grass tops crossing the near foreground, the sky still open above.
cameras.v3: [Tracking shot] Travelling with his legs and feet close, the grass streaming past them at the same constant rate.

composite.where: the open upper half is where scenes 15, 17 and 18 are placed
composite.note: the screenplay's endlose Loop: butt-join the clip to itself to hold the hop for as long as the visions need

17.title: slimy feathers
17.shot1: The feathers of a small Federphibium are wet and beaded with mucus, each feather stuck to the next where the slime has soaked it. The frog sings the line.

cameras.v1: [Zoom in] Pushing onto the slime-soaked feathers.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Wide on the three Federphibien playing on the floor.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] The reverse - the hen watching them from her chair.

composite.where: into the open sky in the upper half of scene 16, half transparent
composite.note: one of the three Zukunftsvisionen - the slime-soaked feathers

18.title: great big eyes
18.shot1: A Federphibium's huge bulging white eyes, each with its small black dot pupil, set wide, blink slowly and heavily. Then a tongue wipes across both of them. The frog sings the line.

cameras.v1: [Zoom in] Pushing onto the huge bulging eyes.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Wide on the whole Federphibium, so the eyes read as part of an animal.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] The reverse - what the eyes are aimed at across the room.

composite.where: into the open sky in the upper half of scene 16, half transparent
composite.note: one of the three Zukunftsvisionen - the huge eyes

19.title: dead in the water
19.lyrics: die nicht zum fliegen oder schwimmen taugen
19.shot1: This is the last image of the daydream and it is the cruel one, so the hybrids are here on purpose: dead Federphibien float in the real pond, backs upward, a dozen of them turning slowly in the duckweed between the lily pads, cattails standing black at the edges of frame and the leaning fence along the far bank behind it all. At the water's edge a man sits on a chair with his back turned, sharpening out of blur as he is approached from behind, until his back and the straw hat above it stand across the front of the frame with the pond beyond him. He never turns.

cameras.v1: [Tracking shot] Low aerial travelling along the pond, side on, ending behind the seated man.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Locked wide on the pond with the floating bodies in it.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Close on one Federphibium floating back upward.

20.title: the researcher's notebook
20.lyrics: Federphibien soll man sie nennen. Nachkömmlinge von Frosch und Hennen
20.shot1: The man's hand smooths down a page of his notebook. On the page is a drawing of a hen and a frog in the manner of a nineteenth century scientific plate, fine pencil work with labelled parts, and beside it the handwritten note "Huhn + Frosch = Federphibium".

cameras.v1: [Static shot] Close on the notebook page and the hand smoothing it.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Wide on the researcher at the pond, seen from behind.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Extreme close on the handwritten note under the drawing.

21.title: skidding onto the gravel
21.shot1: The frog hops off the grass onto sand and gravel and skids to a stop. He turns to one side. Behind him the hen house now stands square on, close and out of focus.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] Worm's eye at gravel level as he skids to a stop.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] High and looking down, which makes the yard large and him small.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Close on the gravel spraying out under him.

22.title: up the chicken ladder
22.shot1: The frog runs up the hen house ladder and disappears through the hole at the top.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] Profile, side on, the ladder and the hole both in frame.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Three-quarter front from below the ladder.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Close on his hands taking the rungs.

23.title: into the down
23.lyrics: Ich deck mich zu mit ihren Daunen
23.shot1: Inside the hen house the frog hops and lands in a heap of down and feathers, which puffs up around him. The hen stands in his way and draws herself up, enormous from where he sits. He sings the line.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] From behind the frog at ground level, the hen towering in front of him.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] High and looking down on both, which flips who is large.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Close on the frog's face tipped up at her.

24.title: the hen shouts him down
24.lyrics: Ich halt sie aus, ihre verrückten Launen
24.shot1: The hen draws breath and shrieks at the frog. He sits in the feather heap facing her, dwarfed, and feathers blow away past him in the blast. One loose feather sails up and covers everything. He sings the line.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] From behind him in the feather heap, feathers blowing away past camera, one covering the lens at the end.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Front on the hen as she draws breath and shrieks.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Close on feathers lifting out of the heap.

25.title: she turns her head
25.shot1: The hen towers over the frog, who is still sitting in the feathers; only the lower part of her body is anywhere near him. She lowers her head down to his level and turns it, so one eye can fix on him directly. He sings the line.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] Close from behind the frog at ground level; only the lower part of the hen's body is in frame until her head comes down into it.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] High and looking down on the pair, the size difference plain.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Extreme close on the hen's eye as it fixes on him.

26.title: reaching behind him
26.lyrics: ... sie schaut mich an. Ich halt’s nicht aus.
26.shot1: Drawn in broad comic style, the frog startles and stiffens with surprise, the hen's lowered head still filling the space in front of him. One frog arm goes back behind him and rummages, as if digging something out of a pocket that is not there. He sings the line.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] From behind the frog, staged broad and flat like a comic panel.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Front on his face, startled and stiff.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Close on the arm rummaging behind his back.

27.title: the ring
27.shot1: The frog's hands hold a small box folded from water lily leaves and open it. Inside, a polished gold ring stands up out of the leaves and catches the light. The hen house wall is soft behind him. He sings the line.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] Close, side on, the hen house wall soft behind the hands and the box.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Three-quarter front, both the box and his face in frame.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Extreme close on the ring standing up out of the leaves.

28.title: she swallows it
28.shot1: The hen pecks the ring up off the leaves in the frog's hands. Her head goes back up and she swallows it, with no reaction at all.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] On the hen as she pecks the ring up and swallows it.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Wide with the frog in frame too, watching it happen.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Extreme close on her throat as it goes down.

29.title: she walks straight past
29.shot1: The hen simply walks past the frog in the feather heap, her feet passing close by him. The frog stays frozen, still staring at the empty air in front of him.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] Side on, the hen's feet huge and out of focus in the foreground as they pass him.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Three-quarter front on the frog, alone in the feathers.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Extreme close on his frozen, unmoving face.

30.title: her walk
30.shot1: The frog turns around. Behind him the hen is walking toward the doorway, her rear rocking slightly left and right. As he turns, the focus travels off him and onto her, and the depth of field shifts with it. He sings the line.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] Front on the frog, the focus travelling off him and onto the hen behind as he turns.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Profile, side on, both of them in the same frame.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Close on the hen's rear rocking as she walks.

31.title: cartoon hearts
31.shot1: The focus travels slowly back off the hen and onto the frog. This is one of only two shots in the film that use a floating symbol: a few flat, hard-edged cartoon hearts rise up above his head, held a moment and gone. The other is the leap out of the hen house, and there are no others.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] The same frame held, focus travelling back onto the frog.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Profile, side on, the hearts rising off the top of frame.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Extreme close on his eyes.

32.title: throwing the grain
32.lyrics: Das macht mich rollig, ich will sie sexen
32.shot1: The frog looks down and finds grain scattered on the ground in front of him. He gathers it up, throws it up over himself, and the grains fall back down toward him. He sings the line.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] Over the frog's shoulder, large in frame, the grain on the ground below him.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Medium wide as he throws the grain up over himself.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Close on the grain falling back down.

33.title: grain on his back
33.lyrics: Ich leg mir Körner auf den Rücken
33.shot1: The grains land on the frog's wet skin and stick to it. Behind him the hen is walking to the door, and at the exact moment the grain lands she stops dead and turns her head. The focus snaps to her as she does. He sings the line.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] Extreme close on the grain landing on wet skin, the focus snapping past him to the hen.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Wide with both of them, the door behind her.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] The reverse - the hen's head turning back toward him.

34.title: she stoops down
34.lyrics: Sie kommt näher, muss sich bücken.
34.shot1: The frog sits in front of the feather heap with his head bowed and grain on his head, neck and back. The hen comes to him and lowers her head down, inspecting the grain. He sings the line.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] Side on and pulled back, the frog in front of the feather heap and the hen coming in.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Three-quarter front, the bowed head and the grain both readable.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Extreme close on the grain on his neck.

35.title: she pecks him
35.lyrics: Sie pickt zärtlich, ich quak leise
35.shot1: The hen starts to peck, once only, gently. At the touch the frog croaks and begins to sweat, single beads standing out on his skin. He sings the line.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] The identical setup to the shot before, held.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Close on the point of contact where the beak meets his skin.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] The reverse - the hen's eye as she pecks.

36.title: their eyes meet
36.lyrics: Jede Berührung schickt mich auf eine Reise
36.shot1: The hen pecks again. The background falls away into flat black and everything slows until only the hen and the frog are left. As she comes down to peck once more the frog looks up, and their eyes meet. He sings the line.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] Holding both of them as the background falls away to flat black.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Close on the frog looking up.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Close on the hen's beak coming down.

37.title: the hen understands
37.shot1: The looks passing between the hen and the frog get more intent. Then it lands with the hen: her pupils suddenly contract to pinpricks.

cameras.v1: [Push in] Close on the hen, pressing in as her pupils contract.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Wide with both of them in the black.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] The reverse - close on the frog holding her look.

38.title: onto her back
38.shot1: The hen turns around and gestures at her own back with her beak. The frog hops up onto it and settles between her wings.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] Wide, both animals fully in frame.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Medium on the hen, chest up, as she gestures at her back.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Insert on the frog settling between her wings.

39.title: running for the door
39.shot1: The hen runs for the doorway with the frog on her back.

cameras.v1: [Zoom in] From behind as she runs for the doorway, pressing in as she goes.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Front on, the pair running straight at camera.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Close on the frog's hands gripping her feathers.

40.title: out of the hen house
40.shot1: Outside the hen house, slow motion takes hold as the hen leaps out of the doorway with the frog on her back, and the same few flat cartoon hearts from earlier swirl around the two of them - the second and last time the film uses them, so a handful, not a shower. At the end the two land on the ground and she runs on, the frog still on her back.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] Wide and side on as the leap carries them out of the doorway in slow motion.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Medium on the pair at the top of the leap.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Insert on the frog's hands gripping her feathers as the leap carries them.

41.title: imagine our children again
41.shot1: The hen keeps running with the frog on her back. The two of them look at each other, besotted, while the background tears past behind them in dust. He sings the line.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] Close and front on, the hen's upper body with the frog visible on her back.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Wide of the two running across open ground.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Close on the ground and dust tearing past beneath them.

42.title: stroking her feathers
42.shot1: The frog strokes the hen's plumage tenderly and leaves a faint trail of slime across it. He closes his eyes and leans against her neck. He sings the line.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] Close on the frog stroking her plumage.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Wide, both of them still running, the gesture small in frame.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Extreme close on the slime trail left across the feathers.

43.title: the researcher stands up
43.lyrics: Die nicht zum fliegen oder schwimmen taugen
43.shot1: The researcher sits at the pond close in front of us, cattails at the frame edges and the sagging chicken-wire fence along the bank behind him, drawing, his back turned and the straw hat brim hiding whatever the shoulders do not. Beyond him the hen and frog run on and blur away as the focus travels back onto him. He jumps up and grabs at the chair to steady it.

cameras.v1: [Zoom out] Widening off the running pair and back onto the researcher, seen from behind.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Low from behind him, the chair tipping and his back filling one side of frame.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Close from behind on his hand catching the chair, the pond beyond.

44.title: photographing them
44.shot1: The researcher, close in front of us and still with his back turned, lifts the old camera hanging at his front and starts shooting out past himself at the hen with the frog on her back, hurried and clumsy, bent over the finder. His face never comes round.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] From behind the researcher as he shoots.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Over his shoulder from behind, the camera held up and the running pair small beyond it.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Close from behind on his hands working the old camera, the black strap taut across his back.

45.title: running on
45.shot1: The hen runs on with the frog on her back, out across open ground, taking a hop over a puddle without breaking stride.
45.shot2: The frog, riding on the hen's back, snatches a fly out of the air with his tongue, an offhand and unhurried catch, and swallows it while she keeps running.

cameras.v1: [Tracking shot] Travelling with the pair across open ground, holding them in the same part of frame.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Locked wide, letting them run through frame and out of it.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Close on the frog riding on her back.

46.title: into the sunset
46.shot1: The day is ending and the sun sits low and warm on the horizon - the one change of light in the film. The hen, with the frog on her back, runs up a shallow hill toward it until only their silhouettes are left against the sky.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] From behind as the two run up the hill into the low sun.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Front on, the pair reduced to silhouettes coming toward camera.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Close on the two silhouetted outlines against the sky.

47.title: the final freeze
47.shot1: The hen jumps, the frog lifts off her back, and the image holds on that pose as a freeze frame, the way an old cartoon ends. Nothing moves.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] Held on the freeze at the top of the jump, nothing moving.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Wide on the frozen pose with the whole landscape around it.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Close on the two of them held mid-air.

composite.note: hold the last frame as long as you like, then close the iris in Resolve - the screenplay asks for the effect there, so it is not rendered in

90.title: hen profile element
90.shot1: An element clip, made only to be laid into the sky of another shot. The hen's head and neck alone, turned to one side so the comb, the wattle and the beak all read against nothing. She holds still, grand and unbothered, and blinks slowly twice. Nothing else is in frame: no body below the neck, no ground, no horizon, no props - only a plain, even field of clear summer blue behind her, edge to edge, the exact blue the empty sky is painted in everywhere else. The field stays perfectly even so the clip can be blended into a sky without a seam showing.

cameras.v1: [Static shot] Locked off, side on, her head and neck filling the middle of the frame with clear space around them.
cameras.v2: [Static shot] Locked off, side on and larger, the head alone.
cameras.v3: [Static shot] Locked off, three-quarter rear, the comb and the back of the neck against the flat field.

composite.where: upper left of the empty sky in scene 14, half transparent
composite.note: no audio and no place on the timeline - hold or loop it to taste. Blend mode over the plate's flat sky; her flat blue field is meant to disappear.
